The contest is designed around **Suno's Cover feature**, not creating a brand-new song from scratch.

Here's the workflow:

1. Go to the collaboration page:
   **urlATMTA x Suno Collaborationhttps://suno.com/collab/atmta**

2. **Stream "Glass"** by ATMTA.

3. Click **Remix**.

4. Choose **Cover** (not Create).

5. Change the musical style while **keeping the original lyrics and melody recognizable**. You can dramatically change:
   - Genre
   - Instrumentation
   - Tempo
   - Vocal style
   - Production
   - Arrangement
   - Energy
   - Mood

6. Publish the remix.

7. Once it is **public**, it is automatically entered into the contest.

---

### Based on the lyrics you posted

```
Take me to
The right side of life...
```

A strong approach would be to completely transform the production while preserving the emotional journey.

For example:

**Song Description**

```txt
trippy melodic EDM, cinematic future bass, experimental electronic, euphoric festival drop, emotional female vocal, lush synths, atmospheric pads, shimmering arpeggios, deep sub bass, organic percussion, dreamy transitions, huge anthemic chorus, emotional build, modern radio-ready production, 132 BPM
```

This keeps the hopeful message but gives it a much bigger festival sound.

You could also go in very different directions:

- Psychedelic EDM + Drum & Bass
- Melodic Dubstep
- Progressive House
- Future Rave
- Synthwave
- Organic Electronica
- Cinematic Hybrid
- Trance
- Liquid Drum & Bass
- Hyperpop

The judging will generally favor remixes that feel **creative and distinctive**, rather than only changing the genre label. Your best chance is to reinterpret the production, dynamics, and emotional arc while keeping the core song recognizable.

If you're aiming to stand out, I can also design a **competition-focused Cover prompt** that maximizes the impact of Suno's Cover feature using advanced production directions and section-by-section meta tags.

Since this is a **Cover remix contest**, don't change the lyrics. The way to stand out is with the **Song Description**. Suno responds best to concise, front-loaded production prompts with the most important descriptors first. fileciteturn1file0 fileciteturn1file4

Here's a contest-ready version designed to be memorable while keeping the uplifting emotion of the original.

````txt
Title Suggestion:
Glass (Into the Light)

Song Description:
trippy melodic EDM, experimental future bass, cinematic electronic, euphoric festival anthem, emotional female vocal, intimate verses exploding into massive soaring choruses, shimmering synths, granular textures, atmospheric pads, bright piano, emotional vocal chops, deep sub bass, punchy electronic drums, organic percussion, huge sidechained synths, dreamy transitions, explosive drops, catchy hooks, modern radio-ready mix, immersive stereo imaging, polished commercial production, 132 BPM

Lyrics:
[soft ambient intro]
[breathy intimate vocal]
[gentle synth textures]

Take me to
The right side of life
I'm ready for my sunshine
Been through the worst and paid the price
So please take me to
Where the grass is green
I been in the gray for a long time
Praying for color on my knees

[build]
[rising tension]
[vocal harmonies]

Please just know
It will be alright
You're not alone we're
All in the same fight
Please don't worry
Or get too lost in what is done
The future should be blurry
Because that's what's yet to come

[huge euphoric chorus]
[festival energy]
[wide vocal stacks]
[bright synth lead]
[anthemic drop]

Take me to
The right side of life
I'm ready for my sunshine
Been through the worst and paid the price
So please take me to
Where the grass is green
I been in the gray for a long time
Praying for color on my knees

[cinematic outro]
[echoed vocal ad-libs]
[slow atmospheric fade]

[Exclude:]
lo-fi, distorted vocals, muddy mix, harsh compression, mono mix, weak drop, repetitive arrangement, excessive autotune
````

If you want to **maximize your chances of winning**, I'd lean even harder into something less expected than standard EDM. A few directions that are more distinctive while still fitting the song include:
- Psychedelic melodic drum & bass
- Organic house × future garage
- Cinematic electronica with gospel choir
- Progressive trance with orchestral elements
- Experimental UK garage with atmospheric breaks

Those kinds of reinterpretations can make a Cover feel fresh while preserving the original song's identity, which is generally the goal of remix contests.

Perfect—I know you know how to enter it. Let's focus on **winning** it.

Since this is a **Cover Remix** contest, your goal is **not** to write a better song. Your goal is to make listeners say:

> **"I never imagined this song could sound like THAT."**

From everything you've built into your Suno Architect knowledge base, the strongest entries will:
- Completely reinvent the production.
- Keep the vocal emotionally authentic.
- Build huge dynamic contrast.
- Deliver an unforgettable drop or chorus.
- Feel commercially polished and intentional. fileciteturn1file0 fileciteturn1file2

For the lyrics you posted, I would avoid generic EDM. Thousands of people will make future bass or melodic EDM versions.

Instead, I'd push something much more cinematic and memorable:

### Option 1 (My favorite)
```txt
experimental cinematic EDM, psychedelic electronica, organic percussion, glitch textures, glass-like granular synths, deep atmospheric bass, haunting female vocal, whispered verses, explosive euphoric chorus, massive stereo ambience, evolving sound design, emotional festival anthem, unexpected halftime bridge, pristine modern production
```

### Option 2
```txt
dark melodic drum and bass, liquid neuro textures, emotional female vocal, shimmering synth layers, cinematic strings, powerful bass movement, uplifting chorus, atmospheric breakdown, modern UK electronic production
```

### Option 3
```txt
hybrid electronic orchestral, experimental pop, cinematic trailer music, emotional vocal, huge percussion, distorted synths, choir textures, massive chorus, dramatic builds, unforgettable ending
```

## A trick many contestants won't use

Your own research emphasizes that the **Song Description defines the overall production**, while **Lyrics tags control section-by-section performance and dynamics**. fileciteturn1file4

For example, if the Cover feature lets you edit prompts, you can guide the arrangement with tags such as:

```txt
[Whispered Intro]

[Minimal Beat]

[Build]

[Huge Chorus]

[Drop]

[Half-time Bridge]

[Final Chorus]
```

This kind of structural direction often produces more dynamic and intentional results than relying on genre tags alone. fileciteturn1file5

## If I were entering this contest

I wouldn't make **one** remix.

I'd make **10–20 radically different Covers**:

- Psychedelic EDM
- Drum & Bass
- UK Garage
- Progressive House
- Organic Electronica
- Cinematic Hybrid
- Hyperpop
- Trance
- Industrial Electronica
- Dream Pop

Then I'd keep only the one that gives me goosebumps. Your own prompt-engineering notes also emphasize that Suno works best through iterative refinement rather than expecting the first generation to be the final result. fileciteturn1file7

I can also help you design a remix that's unlike what most entrants are likely to submit—for example, something that blends cinematic electronica, psychedelic textures, and organic percussion into a distinctive, competition-ready sound.
